benchmarks.verdict: Our gold is substantially more complete than Sol and has no verified factual error (the review agrees: "None of the proposed golds has a load-bearing factual error"). So no corrections. Sol is a generic/conceptual answer whose project-specific facts our gold already contains — with two genuine exceptions: two proxy-validity studies (#5247 and #6096) that our gold does not cite anywhere. Both verified in the frozen corpus with exact numbers matching Sol. These are load-bearing for the "do our proxies actually predict downstream?" half of the question, which our gold currently answers mostly via #5005 (low SNR) and #4389 (negative agentic result) but without the quantified metric-design lesson (#5247) or the pre/post-RL pass@K result (#6096). Recommend adding both as concise sentences in the proxy-validity discussion (near section 4). Framing: Sol's clean lead (targets = capabilities we want to move; proxies = cheap smooth signals read during training) and a compact upfront tier map are worth borrowing to counter the gold's encyclopedic opening — optional, low priority. needs_changes=true on the strength of the two medium additions. additions.item: Proxy-validity study #5247 (Calvin-Xu, 2026-04-28): on the 300M qsplit core rows (n=240), standard MMLU accuracy has essentially no monotonic relation to BPB (Spearman -0.069) and is near-zero vs choice_logprob_norm (-0.026), but MMLU accuracy vs choice_prob_norm correlates +0.866. Close-out reading: 'accuracy is itself noise; just use the smooth proxy w/ the highest SNR.' This is the empirical backbone for why Marin uses soft/normalized-probability + BPB metrics rather than raw accuracy as development proxies. Our gold mentions soft metrics and low SNR (#5005) but never states this quantified metric-design result.
additions.citation: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/5247#issuecomment-4339766407

additions.item: Proxy-validity result #6096 (Helw150): across the 10 SimpleRL-Zoo base models (scored on v5p-8 via Levanter against the published SimpleRL-Zoo accuracy table), base-model reasoning features help predict post-RL level, but predicting the RL gain (post - base) fails (R^2 = 0.33). Close-out interpretation: pre-RL pass@K is the main predictor of post-RL pass@K when other conditions are held fixed; the issue explicitly lists coding/SWE-bench as the untested next domain. Complements our gold's downstream-scaling coverage (#4550) and negative agentic-proxy result (#4389) with a specific post-RL prediction finding not currently cited.
